abstraction_design.rationale: The loader/VM/page abstraction is designed around the app's real variation and makes an Items section nearly pure reuse; small copy-paste (three card builders, two caches, repeated not-found blocks) keeps it from exemplary.

findings.issue: Card view-model construction is duplicated in three places (toCards, loadHome's inline build, loadTeam's member build), so any card-semantics change — e.g. deriving the sprite from the default Pokémon — must be applied three times, and loadHome's species-list source doesn't even carry the data a correct sprite fix needs.
findings.suggestion: Route all card lists through one builder (e.g. extend toCards and give HomeEntry the same shape), and put the sprite URL on the Card VM so the fix has a single home.

findings.issue: The sprite media URL pattern is hardcoded inside a render component while artwork URLs come through the data layer, splitting knowledge of the media scheme across two layers.
findings.suggestion: Have the server data layer supply the sprite URL on the Card VM (as it already does for artwork in loaders.ts:300) and let PokemonCard just render it.

findings.issue: A single 470-line file holds every raw API type, every helper and every page loader; every feature add/remove/edit collides in one file.
findings.suggestion: Split per feature (server/loaders/pokemon.ts, move.ts, …) with loadPageData importing them; the dispatch switch already defines the natural module boundaries.

findings.issue: Two parallel cache implementations (client 60s map here, server TTL map in api-client.ts:18) plus the '/_data' Cache-Control header in server.ts:31 — a caching-policy change touches three spots.
findings.suggestion: Extract one small TTL-cache helper used by both, and document the intended relationship between the three layers' cache rules.

findings.issue: Route path 'types/:name' silently maps to data path '/type/<name>' (singular), an asymmetric convention that must be kept in sync by hand with the switch in loaders.ts:461.
findings.suggestion: Name data kinds to match route segments (or derive the data path from the route config) so the mapping is mechanical.

findings.issue: Title logic depends on the literal resolver key 'data["vm"]' — a future route resolving under a different key silently loses its title.
findings.suggestion: Tag not-found/VM-bearing routes with an explicit data flag (e.g. data: { vmKey: 'vm' }) or resolve under a reserved key documented in one place.

findings.issue: The 'Hidden ability' note and Card.hidden input exist only to serve ability pages, entangling a shared component with one feature's semantics.
findings.suggestion: Keep PokemonCard generic; pass the note text (or a projected suffix) from the ability-page card list.

findings.issue: typeRef label mapping is re-implemented here while an equivalent helper exists in loaders.ts:117 — two places know how a type name becomes a labeled ref.
findings.suggestion: Ship pre-labeled NamedRefs in HomeVM.types (they already are) and reuse a shared helper for lookups.

summary: A well-seamed, current-Angular architecture: pages are dumb VM consumers, the server data layer is the single place data is shaped, and the documented resolver/token/TransferState split makes both fixes and additions predictable. Its main editability liabilities are a single monolithic loaders.ts, card construction duplicated three ways, and a few string conventions (data-path kinds, resolver key, media URL scheme) that couple files implicitly. I'd merge this with the card/sprite consolidation flagged above on the roadmap.
